Consult Summary:
- Adult female with a few days history of a dry, itchy rash on both arms and hands, onset after swimming and with work-related stress; dermatitis is suspected; management discussed includes emollients, topical steroids, and OTC antihistamines; follow-up in 1 week.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry, itchy rash on arms and hands; red skin; started a few days ago; coconut butter used without relief.
- Timeline: Symptoms began a few days ago, after swimming; no improvement with emollients so far; no spread beyond arms/hands; no fever or systemic symptoms.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Swimming may have triggered symptoms; stress at work noted; weather discussed as a potential factor by patient.
- Associated symptoms: No sores, no fever, no sweating, no vomiting, normal appetite and bowel/bladder function.
- Review of systems: No systemic symptoms documented; afebrile; no chest, abdominal, or neurological complaints reported.
- Other clinical notes: Patient is a primary school teacher; stress described as a contributing factor.
- Past Medical History: 
  - Lactose intolerance (mentioned as a possible allergy/history item)
  - Current medication: Microgynon (contraceptive pill); dose/route/frequency not documented
  - No prior skin conditions reported
- Social History:
  - Lives alone
  - Smokes: no
  - Alcohol: no
  - Recreational drugs: no
  - Occupation: primary school teacher
- Family History:
  - Father with asthma
  - Mother with hay fever
  - No known skin problems in family
- Allergies: No explicit allergies documented
- Medications: Microgynon (dose/route/frequency not documented); no other medications
